memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From the Negev he went from place to place until he came to Bethel, to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had been earlier and where he had first built an altar. There Abram called on the name of the Lord. - Gen 13:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram journeys until he arrives at a very particular spot - Bethel, the place where he had pitched his tent and built an altar before he ever went down to Egypt. He returns to the exact place where he last walked closely with God. And there, he "called on the name of the Lord" again.

This is one of the most beautiful pictures of restoration in Scripture. Abram doesn't build a new altar or invent a new approach. He goes back to the old one - back to where he was right with God before the drift began. Restoration usually means returning to what we abandoned, not finding something new.

Perhaps you can identify a "Bethel" in your own life - a season when you walked closely with God, prayed simply, trusted Him honestly. And then somewhere, quietly, you drifted. The way back is to return to that altar. Not to a place on a map, but to the practices and the posture of trust you left behind.

Jesus said to a drifting church, "Consider how far you have fallen! Repent and do the things you did at first" (Rev 2:5). There is no shame in going back. The altar is still there. God is still there. Call on His name again, right where you left off, and begin afresh.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where was your "Bethel" - a time you walked closely with God?
- What did you do "at first" that you need to return to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, take me back to the altar I have left. Restore the simple trust and honest prayer I once had. I call on Your name again today, and I begin afresh with You.
Amen.
